messages:
sam: hi all, new hire here — trying to run `kubectl get pods -n platform-dev` but getting 'Error from server (Forbidden)'. kubeconfig seems to have a dev context but not sure why I'm blocked.

devops-lee: welcome sam! :wave: do `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl config get-contexts --no-headers` so we can see which context is active.

sam: current-context = redwood-dev-sam. get-contexts shows redwood-prod, redwood-staging, redwood-dev-sam (star).

devops-lee: context looks fine. Forbidden usually RBAC. Run `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n platform-dev` and `kubectl auth can-i get namespaces --all-namespaces`.

sam: both return "no".

devops-lee: OK, did you fill out the infra access form? We require the infra form to add you to the eng-newhires group or create a RoleBinding for your idp identity. Link: https://intranet.redwood/onboard/infra-access — choose k8s/dev.

sam: uh i only completed HR onboarding yesterday. will submit now. also my kubeconfig uses SSO exec plugin — any special steps?

devops-lee: exec is expected. The automation works with our idp tokens. After you submit the infra form it kicks an automation job that applies RoleBindings/ClusterRoleBindings. Can take 5-20 minutes.

oncall-bot: access-job queued for user=sam namespaces=[platform-dev] (req=access-99812). Monitor at https://infra.redwood/jobs/access-99812.

sam: submitted. while we wait, is there a safe way to share kubeconfig for debugging without leaking tokens?

devops-lee: yes — run `kubectl config view --minify --flatten > /tmp/sam-kube.yaml` then open and remove the `exec`->`args` / token fields before pasting. Better: use `kubectl --context=redwood-dev-sam auth can-i list pods -n platform-dev` and paste that output only.

kelly: fwiw you can also create a per-project kubeconfig: `kubectl config view --minify --flatten > .kubeconfig` in the repo and set `export KUBECONFIG=$PWD/.kubeconfig:$HOME/.kube/config` or use direnv. prevents accidentally hitting prod.

oncall-bot: access-job access-99812 applied RoleBinding -> ns=platform-dev subject=group:eng-newhires role=view (applied).

sam: checking: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n platform-dev` -> yes. `kubectl get pods -n platform-dev` returns 6 pods. :tada: thanks!

devops-lee: great. last tips: use `kubectx`/`kubens` for quick switching, `kubectl --dry-run=client -f` when applying manifests, and never commit kubeconfigs with exec tokens. If you need elevated perms later, file a review request via the infra form and list the justification + duration.

kelly: also ask your manager to add the GitHub handle in the infra form if you need image pushes to our private registry — separate permission.

sam: saved all links and commands. super helpful, appreciate it! :100:
